- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant stated that after World War II, Poland came under Soviet domination, while Germany was divided into East and West.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant indicated that Germany was reunified in 1990 and Poland regained independence in 1989.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned that Germany and Poland currently have friendly diplomatic relations but still face historical tensions.
- [USER] User inquired about the geographical separation between Germany and Poland.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explained that the modern border is a result of complex historical changes and territorial disputes over centuries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant described the partitioning of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in the late 18th century by Russia, Prussia, and Austria.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant noted that after World War I, Poland regained independence and borders were redrawn, placing ethnic Germans within Poland.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant stated that after World War II, Poland's borders shifted westward, incorporating significant portions of pre-war German territory.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant confirmed that the current border is based on post-World War II agreements, with a length of 467 km.
